skill.name: github-multi-repo
skill.description: Coordinate GitHub repositories, package synchronization, architecture standards, and cross-repository automation with AI-assisted swarm workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate multi-repository GitHub work with dependency sync, architecture checks, testing, and PR automation.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate GitHub multi-repository automation guide, but it contains Bash, gh, git, and npm workflows that can modify repositories, CI, and templates. Many Markdown fence detections are false positives, while the real risks are broad external commands, temporary filesystem operations, hidden configuration writes, and secret access.

remediation.issue: Broad repository mutations through shell and GitHub CLI commands
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit approval gates, dry-run mode, repository allowlists, and branch protection checks before clone, commit, push, or pull request actions.

remediation.issue: Hidden workflow and agent configuration writes
remediation.suggestion: Require security review for .github and .claude changes, and document exactly which files can be created or updated.

remediation.issue: Temporary directory use for repository data and audit output
remediation.suggestion: Use unique workspace-scoped directories, quote shell variables, clean up temporary files, and avoid predictable /tmp paths.

remediation.issue: Webhook secret access in coordination examples
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege secret handling and avoid logging or transmitting secret values outside the intended coordinator.

content.value_statement: Managing changes across many repositories can create drift and missed tests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through coordinated discovery, synchronization, dependency updates, architecture checks, and PR workflows.
actual_capabilities: Discovers related GitHub repositories with gh CLI queries and repository metadata filters.
Coordinates package version alignment, documentation synchronization, and shared configuration updates.
Guides dependency updates with tests, commits, branch creation, and pull request creation.
Defines repository templates, GitHub workflow standards, and cross-repository architecture patterns.
Uses swarm-style agents for coordination, analysis, testing, refactoring, and documentation tasks.
Provides command patterns for dashboards, dependency graphs, health checks, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access and authenticated permissions for each target repository.
Examples assume GitHub, Node.js, npm, jq, git, and claude-flow tooling are available.
Broad repository changes need human review before merge or production deployment.
The skill describes workflows; it does not enforce organization policy by itself.

use_cases.title: Synchronize Service Dependencies
use_cases.description: Update shared packages across many service repositories, run tests, and prepare coordinated pull requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Architecture
use_cases.description: Create shared templates, workflow files, and configuration conventions across a GitHub organization.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Cross-Team Releases
use_cases.description: Track multi-repository changes, assign specialist agents, and report readiness across frontend, backend, and shared libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Map Related Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the github-multi-repo skill to identify related repositories for my organization. Summarize languages, package files, and likely dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Dependency Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the github-multi-repo skill to plan a dependency synchronization across these repositories. Include tests, branches, pull requests, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Project Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the github-multi-repo skill to compare repository structures and propose a standard template for workflows, documentation, and package settings.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate A Security Patch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the github-multi-repo skill to coordinate a security patch across all affected repositories. Require approval before writes and list verification steps.

output_examples.input: Find TypeScript services that need a dependency update.
output_examples.output: A repository list grouped by package usage, update priority, test coverage, and pull request readiness.

output_examples.input: Standardize integration workflows across several repositories.
output_examples.output: A change plan describing target workflow files, branch names, review owners, and validation steps.
A release coordination summary with affected repositories, assigned roles, test status, and merge order.

best_practices: Start with read-only discovery before cloning, editing, or pushing changes.
Use allowlists, small batches, and branch protection for organization-wide operations.
Review generated workflow and configuration changes before opening pull requests.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad update commands against every repository without an allowlist.
Do not push generated workflow changes without security and ownership review.
Do not expose webhook secrets, tokens, or repository data in logs or reports.

faq.question: What tools does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects GitHub CLI, git, npm, jq, claude-flow, and compatible AI tooling such as Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it make repository changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Several workflows describe cloning repositories, editing files, creating branches, pushing commits, and opening pull requests.

faq.question: Is it limited to one repository?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for coordinated work across many related GitHub repositories.

faq.question: Does it handle package synchronization?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for dependency alignment, documentation sync, package updates, testing, and pull requests.

faq.question: What permissions should be used?
faq.answer: Use the least privileged GitHub token or account needed for the selected repositories and operations.

faq.question: Should changes be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review generated commits, workflows, and configuration files before merge or deployment.
